name: Energy meter repeater
summary: Remote register that counts pulses from a transmitting energy meter and repeats its reading at another location.
description: An energy meter repeater has no measuring inputs of its own. It counts pulses from a transmitting meter and displays the resulting energy at a control room or tenant panel, so on the drawing it connects only to a signal circuit rather than to CTs and VTs.

Because it counts pulses, the repeater can drift from the master meter if pulses are lost or the supply is interrupted. The symbol does not show whether it has non-volatile memory or how it is reconciled with the master, which matters if the repeater is used for billing.
readingNotes: Confirm the repeater has no direct measuring inputs.
Check the pulse weight matches the transmitting meter.
distinction: A repeater counts pulses from another meter; a summation meter adds pulses from several meters.
